summary: Frontend E2E of the multi-provider selector (Claude / Gemini / Ollama) + regressions. All bug-fix requirements pass. 1) provider-select is present and switching options updates active-model-label instantly and correctly: Claude -> 'Claude: claude-sonnet-5', Gemini -> 'Gemini: gemini-2.5-flash (non configuré)', Ollama -> 'Ollama (Local): llama3.2:1b'. The label is NO LONGER frozen on claude-sonnet-5. 2) Claude+bash: sending 'Utilise bash: echo TEST_OK' produced the tool-steps-<id> collapsible panel AND 'TEST_OK' in the final response (~3s). 3) Gemini (no key): sending a message surfaces a clear inline error banner 'GEMINI_API_KEY absent. Ajoute ta cle Google AI Studio dans backend/.env (GEMINI_API_KEY=...).' — no crash, no 500 leak (network was 503, handled cleanly). 4) Ollama: 'Dis bonjour' returned a REAL local response ('Bonjour ! Comment puis-je vous aider aujourd'hui ?') within ~30s wait window, no 502. Header stays 'Ollama (Local): llama3.2:1b'. 5) Regression: rename-conv-<id> and feedback-up-<id> still present and interactive. Full action bar (copy/tts/up/down/regenerate/timestamp) rendered on the Ollama assistant message.

issues: Assistant message bubble ALWAYS shows the label '// CLAUDE' even for responses generated by Ollama or Gemini. Since the provider selector now supports 3 backends, this label should reflect the actual provider that produced the message (e.g. '// OLLAMA', '// GEMINI'). Minor cosmetic inconsistency — the tool-steps panel and header (active-model-label) are correct, only the per-message role tag is stale.

action_items: Optional: make the assistant message header (// CLAUDE) dynamic to reflect message.provider instead of being hardcoded.
critical_code_review_comments: The per-message role label '// CLAUDE' appears to be hardcoded in ChatMessage.jsx; it should be derived from message.provider so Ollama/Gemini responses aren't mislabeled.

Gemini 'non configuré' state is displayed both in the header and inside the error banner, which is good UX; consider disabling the send button when the active provider is not configured to prevent an obviously-failing round trip.

success_rate.backend: N/A (validated by main agent via curl)

Ollama first call was ~sub-30s (well within timeout). If a future iteration wants to test the MAX_TOOL_ITERS=25 Claude loop fix, prompt something like 'liste 30 fichiers en utilisant bash 30 fois' — I did not exercise that path here.
